text: What would happen if someone set off a nuke... in space?
Not on a city. Two hundred and fifty miles over your head.
Because right now, US intelligence says Russia is building a satellite that can carry one. And Germany says it could go up as soon as next month.
Here's the crazy part. It wouldn't hurt a single person on the ground... and that's exactly why it's so dangerous.
We know, because America already did it. July, nineteen sixty-two.
In Hawaii, people threw parties on their rooftops to watch.
At eleven p.m., the sky lit up like a brand new sun... then turned blood red.
Nine hundred miles away, three hundred streetlights went dark. Burglar alarms went off. Phone calls between islands just... cut out.
But the real damage was invisible.
The blast left a belt of radiation around Earth for years. Within months, at least six satellites were dead. Including Telstar, the first satellite to beam live TV.
That was nineteen sixty-two. Today, Starlink alone has over eleven thousand satellites up there. Plus the GPS in your phone.
So a nuke in space wouldn't hurt a single person...
it would just turn off the sky your phone talks to.
